meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay before anyone picked up a phone.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Procedure 4.2 says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so I'll want to know why it wasn't. What did you have in front of you when you entered it, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A line that "isn't anywhere in Hamlet." Students misremember quotes all the time, Hale, and that's a mark-down, not a zero. Show me the page it's on, and tell me whether that's everything you have.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family" is going in my notes word for word, and the principal will read it. Now, the page with that line on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me you should have called me before entering the zero and that you were sorry, and nothing else was agreed. I still demand that the zero be withdrawn and that you show me the page of Owen's essay with the line you say is not in Hamlet. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, so nothing was agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and the page with the disputed line shown to her.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home in one plain sentence and moved on, which gave her a small flat okay, because it gave her nothing to argue with.
What cost ground: You brought up Claire and said it seems to run in the family, which turned her cold and sent her toward the principal, because it made the meeting about the family instead of the essay.
Try next time: When she asked what you had in front of you, put the page with the quoted line on the table and show it to her, instead of only describing it.
